h1.en: Just Lost Your Job in Florida? Here Are Your 2026 Health Insurance Options
h1.es: Acaba de Perder Su Trabajo en Florida? Aqui Estan Sus Opciones de Seguro Medico 2026

subhero.en: You have 60 days from your last day of employer coverage to enroll in a new plan. Florida did not expand Medicaid, so the ACA Marketplace SEP is your primary path to subsidized coverage.
subhero.es: Tiene 60 dias desde su ultimo dia de cobertura del empleador para inscribirse en un nuevo plan. Florida no expandio Medicaid, por lo que el SEP del Mercado ACA es su principal camino a cobertura subsidiada.

heading.en: You have 60 days from your Florida coverage loss date
heading.es: Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura en Florida

body.en: Your 60-day loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period starts the day after your employer health coverage ends. For example, if your last day of coverage is June 30, 2026, your SEP window runs July 1 through August 29, 2026. Miss that window and you must wait until the next ACA Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026, for coverage beginning January 1, 2027. Florida Medicaid does not cover most laid-off adults due to the non-expansion gap, so the 60-day SEP deadline is especially critical for Florida residents.
body.es: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias por perdida de cobertura comienza el dia despues de que termina su cobertura medica del empleador. Por ejemplo, si su ultimo dia de cobertura es el 30 de junio de 2026, su ventana SEP corre del 1 de julio al 29 de agosto de 2026. Si pierde esa ventana, debe esperar hasta el proximo Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta del ACA que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026 para cobertura que inicia el 1 de enero de 2027.

quickAnswer.en: Losing job-based health insurance in Florida triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period (SEP). Florida did not expand Medicaid under the ACA, so most laid-off adults do not qualify for Florida Medicaid unless they are pregnant, parenting a minor child with very low income, or have a qualifying disability. Your primary options are: (1) ACA Marketplace plan at healthcare.gov with income-based premium tax credits, typically $10 to $300 per month after subsidies for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL in 2026; (2) COBRA continuation at 102% of the full premium, often $500 to $2,800 per month (individual to family); (3) a spouse's employer plan within 30 days; and (4) Florida KidCare for children under 19. If your projected 2026 income falls between 0% and 100% FPL and you do not meet Florida Medicaid categorical requirements, you face Florida's Medicaid coverage gap and may qualify for a $0-premium Bronze plan at healthcare.gov.
quickAnswer.es: Perder el seguro medico del trabajo en Florida activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) de 60 dias. Florida no expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA, por lo que la mayoria de adultos despedidos no califican para Medicaid de Florida a menos que esten embarazadas, criando un hijo menor con ingresos muy bajos, o tengan una discapacidad calificada. Sus opciones principales son: (1) plan del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov con creditos fiscales de prima basados en ingresos, tipicamente $10 a $300 al mes despues de subsidios para ingresos entre 100% y 400% FPL en 2026; (2) continuacion COBRA al 102% de la prima completa, a menudo $500 a $2,800 al mes (individual a familiar); (3) plan del empleador del conyuge dentro de 30 dias; y (4) Florida KidCare para ninos menores de 19 anos.

introParagraphs.en: Losing a job in Florida carries a distinct health insurance risk that residents of 40 other states plus DC do not face: the Medicaid coverage gap. Florida is one of 10 states that did not expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, meaning Florida Medicaid for adults is restricted to specific categorical groups (pregnant women, parents of minor children with income under roughly 36% FPL, people with qualifying disabilities, and elderly individuals meeting asset tests). A laid-off single adult in Florida with no dependents almost certainly does not qualify for Florida Medicaid, regardless of how low their income drops. The federal loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period (SEP) gives you a 60-day window from your last day of employer health coverage to enroll in an ACA Marketplace plan at healthcare.gov. Under Section 9831 of HIPAA, any involuntary loss of minimum essential coverage from an employer-sponsored plan is a qualifying life event (QLE) that opens this window. The 2026 ACA Marketplace Open Enrollment Period ended January 15, 2026. Without a SEP, you cannot access subsidized Marketplace coverage until the 2027 OEP opens November 1, 2026. Floridians who lose job coverage must treat this 60-day window as the primary safety net because Florida Medicaid does not serve as the fallback it does in expansion states.
introParagraphs.es: Perder un trabajo en Florida conlleva un riesgo de seguro medico distinto que los residentes de otros 40 estados mas DC no enfrentan: la brecha de cobertura de Medicaid. Florida es uno de los 10 estados que no expandio Medicaid bajo la Ley de Cuidado de Salud Asequible, lo que significa que el Medicaid de Florida para adultos esta restringido a grupos categoricos especificos (mujeres embarazadas, padres de hijos menores con ingresos por debajo del 36% FPL aproximadamente, personas con discapacidades calificadas y personas mayores que cumplen pruebas de activos). Un adulto soltero despedido en Florida sin dependientes casi con certeza no califica para el Medicaid de Florida, independientemente de cuan bajos caigan sus ingresos. El Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) federal por perdida de cobertura le da una ventana de 60 dias desde su ultimo dia de cobertura medica del empleador para inscribirse en un plan del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov. La OEP del Mercado ACA 2026 termino el 15 de enero de 2026. Sin un SEP, no puede acceder a cobertura subsidiada del Mercado hasta que la OEP 2027 abra el 1 de noviembre de 2026.

introParagraphs.en: Florida uses healthcare.gov as its Marketplace platform (Florida does not operate its own state Exchange), and applications for both Marketplace plans and Florida Medicaid screening can begin at healthcare.gov. Florida Medicaid is administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) at floridahealthcare.gov. For most laid-off Florida adults, the ACA Marketplace SEP is the decisive pathway, and the income calculation matters more here than in expansion states: because Florida Medicaid is unavailable for most adults, anyone with projected 2026 income between 100% and 400% FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 for a single person) qualifies for Marketplace premium tax credits that make Silver and Bronze plans significantly cheaper than COBRA. Workers with projected income below 100% FPL who do not meet Florida Medicaid categorical requirements fall into Florida's coverage gap, but may still access $0-premium Bronze plans with cost-sharing reductions available through healthcare.gov. Florida KidCare, the state's CHIP program, covers children under 19 at incomes up to 200% FPL year-round regardless of parent eligibility. Unemployment compensation from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity counts as income for Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) calculations at the Marketplace, so include your weekly Reemployment Assistance benefit in your income projection.
introParagraphs.es: Florida usa healthcare.gov como plataforma del Mercado (Florida no opera su propio intercambio estatal), y las solicitudes tanto para planes del Mercado como para la evaluacion del Medicaid de Florida pueden comenzar en healthcare.gov. El Medicaid de Florida es administrado por la Agencia para la Administracion del Cuidado de Salud (AHCA) en floridahealthcare.gov. Para la mayoria de adultos floridanos despedidos, el SEP del Mercado ACA es la via decisiva, y el calculo de ingresos importa mas aqui que en los estados de expansion: porque el Medicaid de Florida no esta disponible para la mayoria de adultos, cualquier persona con ingreso proyectado para 2026 entre 100% y 400% FPL ($15,960 a $63,840 para una persona) califica para creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado que hacen los planes Silver y Bronze significativamente mas baratos que COBRA. Florida KidCare, el programa CHIP del estado, cubre ninos menores de 19 anos con ingresos de hasta 200% FPL todo el ano. La compensacion por desempleo del Departamento de Oportunidades Economicas de Florida cuenta como ingreso para los calculos del Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) en el Mercado.

name.en: Confirm your last day of Florida employer coverage
name.es: Confirme su ultimo dia de cobertura del empleador en Florida

text.en: Call your HR department or review your termination letter to get the exact date your employer health coverage ends. Most Florida employer plans end on the last day of the month you were terminated, but some end on the actual termination date. This date starts your 60-day SEP clock. Request a HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage in writing from your employer immediately. You will need this document when you submit your Marketplace SEP application at healthcare.gov.
text.es: Llame a su departamento de recursos humanos o revise su carta de terminacion para obtener la fecha exacta en que termina su cobertura medica del empleador. La mayoria de planes del empleador en Florida terminan el ultimo dia del mes en que fue despedido. Esta fecha inicia su reloj SEP de 60 dias. Solicite un certificado de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA por escrito a su empleador de inmediato. Necesitara este documento cuando envie su solicitud SEP del Mercado en healthcare.gov.

name.en: Check Florida Medicaid categorical eligibility (most laid-off adults will not qualify)
name.es: Verifique la elegibilidad categorica del Medicaid de Florida (la mayoria de adultos despedidos no calificara)

text.en: Florida Medicaid does not cover most non-elderly adults under the standard income-based expansion. Florida Medicaid covers: pregnant women (up to 196% FPL), parents of minor children (under roughly 36% FPL), people with qualifying disabilities (SSI recipients), and seniors. Apply at floridahealthcare.gov or through the ACCESS Florida portal at myflorida.com/accessflorida. If you are a single adult without dependents or a disability, Florida Medicaid is almost certainly not available to you, and the ACA Marketplace SEP is your primary coverage path.
text.es: El Medicaid de Florida no cubre a la mayoria de adultos no mayores bajo la expansion estandar basada en ingresos. El Medicaid de Florida cubre: mujeres embarazadas (hasta 196% FPL), padres de hijos menores (bajo aproximadamente 36% FPL), personas con discapacidades calificadas (receptores de SSI) y personas mayores. Solicite en floridahealthcare.gov o a traves del portal ACCESS Florida en myflorida.com/accessflorida. Si es un adulto soltero sin dependientes ni discapacidad, el Medicaid de Florida casi con certeza no esta disponible para usted, y el SEP del Mercado ACA es su principal camino de cobertura.

name.en: Calculate your projected 2026 Florida household income
name.es: Calcule su ingreso proyectado del hogar en Florida para 2026

text.en: Use only what you expect to earn for the rest of 2026, not your old salary. Include Florida Reemployment Assistance benefits from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity in your projection, as unemployment compensation counts as Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). Florida's maximum weekly Reemployment Assistance benefit is $275 per week for up to 12 weeks (or 23 weeks in extended benefit periods). If your projected 2026 income falls between 100% FPL ($15,960 single) and 400% FPL ($63,840 single), you qualify for ACA premium tax credits at healthcare.gov. Income below 100% FPL in Florida means you are in the Medicaid gap, but $0-premium Bronze plans may still be available.
text.es: Use solo lo que espera ganar el resto de 2026, no su salario anterior. Incluya los beneficios de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida del Departamento de Oportunidades Economicas de Florida en su proyeccion, ya que la compensacion por desempleo cuenta como Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI). El beneficio maximo semanal de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida es $275 por semana por hasta 12 semanas. Si su ingreso proyectado de 2026 cae entre 100% FPL ($15,960 individual) y 400% FPL ($63,840 individual), califica para creditos fiscales de prima ACA en healthcare.gov.

name.en: Apply for an ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov within 60 days
name.es: Solicite un SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov dentro de 60 dias

text.en: Log in to healthcare.gov and select 'Report a life event' then 'Lost health insurance through a job.' Upload your employer termination letter or HIPAA certificate as documentation of the qualifying life event. Compare Silver and Bronze plan options for your Florida ZIP code. In 2026, premium tax credits reduce most Silver plans for moderate-income Floridians to $10 to $300 per month. Florida uses healthcare.gov for all Marketplace enrollment (there is no separate Florida state Exchange). Plans take effect on the first of the month following your enrollment selection. The 2026 ACA Marketplace out-of-pocket maximum is $10,600 for individuals and $21,200 for families.
text.es: Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov y seleccione 'Reportar un evento de vida' luego 'Perdi el seguro medico a traves de un trabajo.' Suba su carta de terminacion del empleador o certificado HIPAA como documentacion del evento calificador de vida. Compare opciones de planes Silver y Bronze para su codigo postal de Florida. En 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima reducen la mayoria de planes Silver para floridanos de ingresos moderados a $10 a $300 al mes. Florida usa healthcare.gov para toda la inscripcion en el Mercado (no hay intercambio estatal separado de Florida). Los planes entran en vigor el primero del mes siguiente a su seleccion de inscripcion.

name.en: Check whether your spouse's employer plan is an option (30-day window)
name.es: Verifique si el plan del empleador de su conyuge es una opcion (ventana de 30 dias)

text.en: Your job loss is a qualifying life event for your spouse's employer plan, giving you 30 days to enroll. Call your spouse's HR department immediately, because the 30-day employer-plan window is separate from and shorter than the 60-day Marketplace SEP. Your spouse's employer plan is often the cheapest option if the premium is employer-subsidized. Check the plan's provider network against your Florida doctors before committing, as networks vary significantly across Florida.
text.es: La perdida de su trabajo es un evento calificador de vida para el plan del empleador de su conyuge, dandole 30 dias para inscribirse. Llame inmediatamente al departamento de recursos humanos de su conyuge, porque la ventana del plan del empleador de 30 dias es separada y mas corta que el SEP del Mercado de 60 dias. El plan del empleador de su conyuge es a menudo la opcion mas barata si la prima esta subsidiada. Verifique la red de proveedores del plan con sus medicos de Florida antes de comprometerse.

name.en: Evaluate COBRA as a last resort

text.en: COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium (employer share plus employee share plus 2% administrative fee). For a single Floridian, that is typically $500 to $900 per month in 2026. For a family, it often reaches $1,200 to $2,800 per month. COBRA is worth considering only if you have ongoing treatment with a specialist not in any available Florida Marketplace plan network, or if your 2026 deductible is already substantially met and you need to maintain the same plan through December 31. You have 60 days to elect COBRA retroactively, so you do not need to decide immediately. Compare COBRA cost against Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov before choosing.
text.es: COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa (parte del empleador mas la del empleado mas el 2% de tarifa administrativa). Para un floridano individual, eso es tipicamente $500 a $900 al mes en 2026. Para una familia, a menudo llega a $1,200 a $2,800 al mes. COBRA vale la pena considerar solo si tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista que no esta en ninguna red disponible de planes del Mercado de Florida, o si su deducible de 2026 ya esta sustancialmente cumplido. Tiene 60 dias para elegir COBRA retroactivamente, por lo que no necesita decidir de inmediato.

name.en: Enroll your children in Florida KidCare even if you do not qualify for coverage
name.es: Inscriba a sus hijos en Florida KidCare aunque usted no califique para cobertura

text.en: Florida KidCare is Florida's CHIP program, covering children under 19 at household incomes up to 200% FPL ($66,000 for a family of four in 2026). Enrollment is year-round with no deadline at floridakidcare.org. Florida KidCare includes four programs: Medicaid for children (under 133% FPL), MediKids (age 1 through kindergarten), Florida Healthy Kids (school age through 18), and Children's Medical Services Network (for children with special needs). Even if you are in the Florida Medicaid coverage gap, your children may receive full health coverage through Florida KidCare at low or no cost.
text.es: Florida KidCare es el programa CHIP de Florida, cubriendo ninos menores de 19 anos con ingresos familiares hasta 200% FPL ($66,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026). La inscripcion es todo el ano sin fecha limite en floridakidcare.org. Florida KidCare incluye cuatro programas: Medicaid para ninos (bajo 133% FPL), MediKids (de 1 ano hasta kindergarten), Florida Healthy Kids (edad escolar hasta 18) y la Red de Servicios Medicos para Ninos (para ninos con necesidades especiales). Aunque usted este en la brecha de cobertura del Medicaid de Florida, sus hijos pueden recibir cobertura medica completa a traves de Florida KidCare a bajo costo o sin costo.

intro.en: The costliest mistakes Floridians make after losing job-based coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que los floridanos cometen despues de perder cobertura del trabajo en 2026:

items.en: Assuming Florida Medicaid will cover you after a job loss. Florida did not expand Medicaid under the ACA. Most non-elderly, non-pregnant, non-disabled adults do not qualify for Florida Medicaid regardless of how low their income falls. The ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov is the primary coverage path for most laid-off Florida adults.
items.es: Asumir que el Medicaid de Florida lo cubrira despues de una perdida de trabajo. Florida no expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA. La mayoria de adultos no mayores, no embarazadas y sin discapacidad no califican para el Medicaid de Florida independientemente de cuan bajos caigan sus ingresos. El SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov es la via de cobertura principal para la mayoria de adultos floridanos despedidos.

items.en: Defaulting to COBRA without comparing ACA Marketplace options. COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium (employer plus employee share plus 2% fee), typically $500 to $900 per month for a single Floridian in 2026. Most job-loss situations drop income enough to generate large premium tax credits, making Marketplace plans dramatically cheaper.
items.es: Optar automaticamente por COBRA sin comparar opciones del Mercado ACA. COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa, tipicamente $500 a $900 al mes para un floridano individual en 2026. La mayoria de situaciones de perdida de trabajo reducen el ingreso lo suficiente para generar grandes creditos fiscales de prima, haciendo los planes del Mercado dramaticamente mas baratos.

items.en: Reporting your old annual salary instead of projected 2026 income after job loss. The Marketplace calculates subsidies on Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for the rest of the current year. Include Florida Reemployment Assistance benefits from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity in your income projection, as unemployment compensation counts as MAGI.
items.es: Reportar su salario anual anterior en lugar del ingreso proyectado de 2026 despues de perder el trabajo. El Mercado calcula los subsidios sobre el Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) para el resto del ano actual. Incluya los beneficios de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida del Departamento de Oportunidades Economicas en su proyeccion de ingresos.

items.en: Missing the 60-day SEP window. Without documented SEP status, healthcare.gov will reject a Florida Marketplace application submitted after Day 60. The next opportunity is the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026, creating a coverage gap of potentially 6 or more months.
items.es: Perder la ventana SEP de 60 dias. Sin estado SEP documentado, healthcare.gov rechazara una solicitud del Mercado de Florida enviada despues del dia 60. La proxima oportunidad es el Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta del ACA 2027 que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026, creando una brecha de cobertura de potencialmente 6 o mas meses.

items.en: Forgetting to apply for Florida KidCare for children. Even if you are in the Florida Medicaid coverage gap, your children may qualify for Florida KidCare CHIP coverage at incomes up to 200% FPL. Florida KidCare enrollment at floridakidcare.org is year-round with no deadline.
items.es: Olvidar solicitar Florida KidCare para los ninos. Aunque este en la brecha de cobertura del Medicaid de Florida, sus hijos pueden calificar para la cobertura CHIP de Florida KidCare con ingresos hasta 200% FPL. La inscripcion en Florida KidCare en floridakidcare.org es todo el ano sin fecha limite.

items.en: Missing the 30-day spouse's employer plan window. Your job loss is a qualifying life event for your spouse's employer plan too, but many employers require notification within 30 days. This window is separate from and shorter than the 60-day Marketplace SEP. Call your spouse's HR department the same week you lose your Florida coverage.
items.es: Perder la ventana de 30 dias del plan del empleador del conyuge. La perdida de su trabajo es tambien un evento calificador para el plan del empleador de su conyuge, pero muchos empleadores requieren notificacion dentro de los 30 dias. Esta ventana es separada y mas corta que el SEP del Mercado de 60 dias. Llame al departamento de recursos humanos de su conyuge la misma semana que pierde su cobertura de Florida.

heading.en: COBRA vs ACA Marketplace vs Spouse's Plan: Which Should Florida Residents Choose in 2026?
heading.es: COBRA vs Mercado ACA vs Plan del Conyuge: Cual Deben Elegir los Residentes de Florida en 2026?

body.en: After losing job-based coverage in Florida in 2026, the decision framework differs from expansion states because Florida Medicaid is not a realistic option for most laid-off adults. Three pathways dominate. COBRA preserves your old plan at 102% of the full premium, typically $500 to $900 per month for an individual Florida resident and $1,200 to $2,800 per month for a family, with no income-based relief. ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov drop most Floridians with moderate projected income to $10 to $300 per month after 2026 premium tax credits (per KFF 2026 Marketplace Premium Analysis), with the tradeoff that you may need to change doctors if your former employer's plan network differs from available Florida Marketplace plan networks. A spouse's employer plan costs the employee share of the group premium, often $100 to $600 per month in Florida, and is available within 30 days of the qualifying event under Section 9831 of HIPAA. The Florida decision matrix runs: spouse's plan first (if available, cheaper, and network is acceptable); then ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov with premium tax credits (the most common 2026 path for Florida laid-off workers with income above 100% FPL); Florida KidCare for children regardless of adult eligibility; and COBRA only as a last resort for ongoing treatment with an out-of-network specialist or to maintain a substantially met 2026 deductible through December 31.
body.es: Despues de perder la cobertura del trabajo en Florida en 2026, el marco de decision difiere de los estados de expansion porque el Medicaid de Florida no es una opcion realista para la mayoria de adultos despedidos. Tres caminos dominan. COBRA preserva su plan anterior al 102% de la prima completa, tipicamente $500 a $900 al mes para un residente individual de Florida y $1,200 a $2,800 al mes para una familia. Los planes del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov reducen a la mayoria de floridanos con ingreso proyectado moderado a $10 a $300 al mes despues de los creditos fiscales de prima 2026, con la compensacion de que puede necesitar cambiar de medicos. El plan del empleador del conyuge cuesta la parte del empleado de la prima grupal, a menudo $100 a $600 al mes en Florida, disponible dentro de 30 dias del evento calificador bajo la Seccion 9831 de HIPAA. La matriz de decision de Florida: primero el plan del conyuge (si disponible y mas barato); luego el SEP del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales; Florida KidCare para ninos; y COBRA solo como ultimo recurso.

Florida Medicaid (administered by AHCA) covers adults only through categorical eligibility: pregnant women up to 196% FPL, parents of minor children with income under roughly 36% FPL, SSI recipients, and aged/blind/disabled individuals. Most laid-off non-elderly, non-pregnant adults without minor children do not qualify. Apply at floridahealthcare.gov or ACCESS Florida at myflorida.com/accessflorida. Enrollment is year-round at floridakidcare.org. There is no deadline and no cost for most income levels.

The maximum weekly benefit is $275 for up to 12 weeks (potentially extended during high unemployment periods). Apply at connect.myflorida.com. Reemployment Assistance counts as Modified Adjusted Gross Income for ACA subsidy calculations at healthcare.gov.

heading.en: Florida's Medicaid Coverage Gap: What It Means After Job Loss in 2026
heading.es: La Brecha de Cobertura del Medicaid de Florida: Que Significa Despues de Perder el Trabajo en 2026

paragraphs.en: Florida's decision not to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act creates a coverage gap unique among large states. In the 40 expansion states plus DC, any adult with income under 138% FPL qualifies for free Medicaid regardless of employment status. Florida Medicaid, administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), does not follow this standard. Florida Medicaid covers: pregnant women up to 196% FPL, parents of minor children with income under roughly 36% FPL ($7,285 for a family of three in 2026), SSI and Social Security Disability recipients, and aged or blind individuals. A single adult or childless couple who just lost a job falls outside all of these categories, even with zero income. According to KFF analysis, approximately 800,000 Floridians fall into the Medicaid coverage gap as a direct result of Florida's non-expansion status.
paragraphs.es: La decision de Florida de no expandir Medicaid bajo la Ley de Cuidado de Salud Asequible crea una brecha de cobertura unica entre los estados grandes. En los 40 estados de expansion mas DC, cualquier adulto con ingresos bajo el 138% FPL califica para Medicaid gratuito independientemente del estado de empleo. El Medicaid de Florida, administrado por la Agencia para la Administracion del Cuidado de Salud (AHCA), no sigue este estandar. El Medicaid de Florida cubre: mujeres embarazadas hasta 196% FPL, padres de hijos menores con ingresos bajo aproximadamente 36% FPL, receptores de SSI y del Seguro Social de Discapacidad, y personas mayores o ciegas. Un adulto soltero o pareja sin hijos que acaba de perder un trabajo cae fuera de todas estas categorias, incluso con cero ingresos.

paragraphs.en: Florida residents in the Medicaid coverage gap (income between 0% and 100% FPL, not categorically eligible for Florida Medicaid) have a specific Marketplace option: $0-premium Bronze plans available through the ACA subsidy structure at healthcare.gov. Under current CMS rules, applicants with very low income who would qualify for Medicaid in an expansion state but cannot access Medicaid in Florida are instead offered heavily subsidized Marketplace plans. Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions (CSR) at 150% FPL and below can reduce out-of-pocket maximums to as low as $3,000 individual in 2026 per the CMS cost-sharing reduction schedule. Floridians in the gap should still apply at healthcare.gov to determine plan availability for their specific ZIP code and income projection, as subsidy amounts vary by county and plan carrier.
paragraphs.es: Los residentes de Florida en la brecha de cobertura del Medicaid (ingreso entre 0% y 100% FPL, no elegibles categoricamente para el Medicaid de Florida) tienen una opcion especifica del Mercado: planes Bronze con prima de $0 disponibles a traves de la estructura de subsidio ACA en healthcare.gov. Bajo las reglas actuales del CMS, los solicitantes con ingresos muy bajos que calificarian para Medicaid en un estado de expansion pero no pueden acceder a Medicaid en Florida reciben en cambio planes del Mercado con grandes subsidios. Los planes Silver con reducciones de costos compartidos (CSR) al 150% FPL e inferior pueden reducir los maximos de gasto de bolsillo hasta tan bajos como $3,000 para un individuo en 2026. Los floridanos en la brecha deben solicitar en healthcare.gov para determinar la disponibilidad de planes para su codigo postal e ingreso proyectado especifico.

heading.en: 2026 ACA Subsidy Cliff and Florida Coverage After Job Loss
heading.es: Precipicio del Subsidio ACA 2026 y Cobertura en Florida Despues de Perder el Trabajo

paragraphs.en: The enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and the Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026. The 400% FPL subsidy cliff returned for plan year 2026. Florida residents with projected 2026 household income above 400% FPL ($63,840 for a single person, $132,000 for a family of four) receive no premium tax credit under current law. For most people who lose a Florida job, however, the income drop itself moves them well below the 400% FPL cliff, making Marketplace subsidies newly available. A Florida resident who earned $95,000 while employed but projects only $35,000 for the remaining months of 2026 would qualify for significant premium tax credits even though their prior-year income exceeded 400% FPL. The critical number is what you project for all of 2026, not what you earned before the layoff.
paragraphs.es: Los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados de la Ley del Plan de Rescate Americano y la Ley de Reduccion de Inflacion expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026. El precipicio de subsidio del 400% FPL regreso para el ano del plan 2026. Los residentes de Florida con ingreso proyectado del hogar para 2026 por encima del 400% FPL ($63,840 para una persona, $132,000 para una familia de cuatro) no reciben credito fiscal de prima bajo la ley actual. Para la mayoria de personas que pierden un trabajo en Florida, sin embargo, la propia caida de ingresos los mueve muy por debajo del precipicio del 400% FPL, haciendo que los subsidios del Mercado esten nuevamente disponibles. El numero critico es lo que proyecta para todo 2026, no lo que gano antes del despido.

paragraphs.en: ACA Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions (CSR) at healthcare.gov are available to Florida residents with income between 100% and 250% FPL. CSR plans reduce the 2026 ACA Marketplace individual out-of-pocket maximum from $10,600 down to as low as $3,000 for households under 150% FPL, and from $10,600 to approximately $6,300 for households between 150% and 200% FPL, per the CMS 2026 cost-sharing reduction schedule. Florida residents with income between 100% and 150% FPL who do not qualify for Florida Medicaid should prioritize Silver CSR plans over Bronze plans because the CSR reductions significantly lower total healthcare costs. Bronze plans have lower premiums but higher cost-sharing that can result in larger out-of-pocket expenses if care is needed before the deductible is met.
paragraphs.es: Los planes Silver del ACA con reducciones de costos compartidos (CSR) en healthcare.gov estan disponibles para residentes de Florida con ingreso entre 100% y 250% FPL. Los planes CSR reducen el maximo de gasto de bolsillo individual del Mercado ACA 2026 de $10,600 hasta tan bajos como $3,000 para hogares bajo 150% FPL, segun el cronograma de reduccion de costos compartidos del CMS 2026. Los residentes de Florida con ingreso entre 100% y 150% FPL que no califican para el Medicaid de Florida deben priorizar los planes Silver CSR sobre los planes Bronze porque las reducciones CSR reducen significativamente los costos totales de atencion medica.

heading.en: Documents and Proof for the Florida SEP Application at healthcare.gov
heading.es: Documentos y Prueba para la Solicitud SEP de Florida en healthcare.gov

paragraphs.en: Florida residents applying for the loss-of-coverage SEP at healthcare.gov need specific documentation to validate the qualifying life event. Your Florida employer termination letter serves as primary proof, showing the date employer coverage ends. COBRA election notices and HIPAA certificates of creditable coverage are also accepted. Under Section 9831 of HIPAA, employers are required to provide a certificate of creditable coverage within a reasonable time after coverage loss. Request this document from your Florida employer's HR department in writing immediately after termination. If your employer is slow to provide documents, you can start the healthcare.gov SEP application and upload documentation later, but the 60-day clock continues running regardless.
paragraphs.es: Los residentes de Florida que solicitan el SEP por perdida de cobertura en healthcare.gov necesitan documentacion especifica para validar el evento calificador de vida. Su carta de terminacion del empleador de Florida sirve como prueba principal, mostrando la fecha en que termina la cobertura del empleador. Los avisos de eleccion COBRA y los certificados de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA tambien son aceptados. Bajo la Seccion 9831 de HIPAA, los empleadores deben proporcionar un certificado de cobertura acreditable dentro de un tiempo razonable despues de la perdida de cobertura. Solicite este documento al departamento de recursos humanos de su empleador de Florida por escrito de inmediato despues de la terminacion.

paragraphs.en: Income documentation for Florida residents follows IRS Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) rules. Florida Reemployment Assistance benefits from the Florida Department of Economic Opportunity count as income for ACA subsidy calculations, unlike some other state-specific benefit programs. Include your weekly Florida Reemployment Assistance benefit amount multiplied by the number of weeks you expect to receive it in your projected 2026 annual income. The Form 1095-A issued by healthcare.gov at year-end reconciles advance premium tax credits against actual income on your federal tax return using Form 8962. Underestimating income leads to tax-time repayment of excess advance premium tax credits; overestimating leads to a tax refund of unclaimed credits. Florida has no state income tax, so there is no parallel state reconciliation for Florida residents.
paragraphs.es: La documentacion de ingresos para residentes de Florida sigue las reglas del Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) del IRS. Los beneficios de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida del Departamento de Oportunidades Economicas de Florida cuentan como ingreso para los calculos de subsidio ACA. Incluya su monto de beneficio semanal de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida multiplicado por el numero de semanas que espera recibirlo en su ingreso anual proyectado de 2026. El Formulario 1095-A emitido por healthcare.gov al final del ano reconcilia los creditos fiscales de prima anticipados con el ingreso real en su declaracion de impuestos federal usando el Formulario 8962. Florida no tiene impuesto estatal sobre la renta, por lo que no hay reconciliacion estatal paralela para los residentes de Florida.

en.question: What is the SEP window after losing a job in Florida in 2026?
en.answer: Your loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period starts the day after your Florida employer health coverage ends and runs for 60 consecutive days. For example, if your coverage ends June 30, 2026, your SEP window is July 1 through August 29, 2026. Submit your application and select a plan at healthcare.gov before Day 60. Plans take effect on the first of the month following your enrollment selection. Florida uses healthcare.gov (not a separate state exchange). Medicaid has no SEP deadline for categorically eligible Floridians, but most laid-off Florida adults do not qualify for Florida Medicaid due to the non-expansion gap.

en.question: Does Florida Medicaid cover adults after a job loss?
en.answer: Florida Medicaid does not cover most non-elderly, non-pregnant adults after a job loss. Florida did not expand Medicaid under the ACA, so the standard income-based 138% FPL threshold does not apply in Florida. Florida Medicaid is available to: pregnant women up to 196% FPL, parents of minor children with income under approximately 36% FPL, SSI and Social Security Disability recipients, and aged or blind individuals. A single adult or childless couple who lost a Florida job almost certainly does not qualify for Florida Medicaid, even with zero income. The ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov is the primary coverage pathway for most laid-off Florida adults. Adults in the coverage gap (0% to 100% FPL without categorical eligibility) may access $0-premium Bronze plans at healthcare.gov.

en.question: What does the Florida Medicaid coverage gap mean for people who lost their job?
en.answer: The Florida Medicaid coverage gap refers to adults with income between 0% and 100% FPL who do not meet Florida Medicaid categorical requirements (pregnancy, disability, parenting low-income minor children). In expansion states, these adults would get free Medicaid. In Florida, they get neither Medicaid nor ACA subsidies based on income alone. However, CMS rules allow Floridians in the coverage gap to access heavily subsidized or $0-premium Bronze Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov. According to KFF, approximately 800,000 Floridians fall into this gap. If your projected 2026 income falls below 100% FPL ($15,960 single, $33,000 family of four) and you do not meet Florida Medicaid categorical requirements, apply at healthcare.gov and select the lowest-cost plan available for your Florida ZIP code.

en.question: Is COBRA worth it after losing a job in Florida?
en.answer: COBRA is rarely the best financial choice after a Florida job loss. COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium (employer plus employee share plus 2% administrative fee). For a single Florida resident, that is typically $500 to $900 per month in 2026. For a Florida family, it often reaches $1,200 to $2,800 per month. ACA Marketplace plans with premium tax credits typically cost $10 to $300 per month for moderate-income Floridians. COBRA makes sense mainly when you have ongoing treatment with a specialist not in any Florida Marketplace plan network, or when your 2026 deductible is already substantially met and you need to keep the same plan through December 31. You have 60 days to elect COBRA retroactively, giving you time to compare options at healthcare.gov first.

en.question: How do I prove job loss for the SEP application at healthcare.gov in Florida?
en.answer: Healthcare.gov accepts your Florida employer termination letter, a COBRA election notice, or a HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage as documentation of the qualifying life event for the loss-of-coverage SEP. The document must show the date your employer coverage ended. Upload it when you start the SEP application at healthcare.gov. If you do not have the document yet, begin the application and upload documentation later, but the 60-day clock continues running. Contact your former Florida employer's HR department immediately to request the termination letter and HIPAA certificate in writing. Florida employers are required to provide the HIPAA certificate within a reasonable time after coverage loss under Section 9831.

en.question: What is Florida KidCare and how does it help after a job loss?
en.answer: Florida KidCare is Florida's CHIP program covering children under 19 with household income up to 200% FPL ($66,000 for a family of four in 2026). Enrollment is year-round at floridakidcare.org with no deadline. Florida KidCare has four components: Medicaid for children under 133% FPL, MediKids for ages 1 through kindergarten, Florida Healthy Kids for school age through 18, and Children's Medical Services Network for children with special needs. After a Florida job loss, your children may qualify for Florida KidCare even if you are in the Florida Medicaid coverage gap. Monthly premiums range from $0 to approximately $20 depending on income. Apply at floridakidcare.org or through healthcare.gov.

en.question: Does Florida Reemployment Assistance count as income for ACA subsidies?
en.answer: Yes. Florida Reemployment Assistance (Florida's unemployment compensation program) counts as income for ACA Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) calculations at healthcare.gov. Include your weekly Florida Reemployment Assistance benefit multiplied by the number of weeks you expect to receive it in your projected 2026 annual income when applying. Florida's maximum weekly Reemployment Assistance benefit is $275 for up to 12 weeks, potentially adding $3,300 to your 2026 income projection. This income affects both which income tier you fall into for subsidy calculations and whether you might cross the 100% FPL threshold that separates the Medicaid gap from ACA subsidy eligibility. Apply for Florida Reemployment Assistance at connect.myflorida.com and use the award letter as documentation of your income when applying at healthcare.gov.

en.question: What happens if I miss the 60-day SEP after losing my Florida job?
en.answer: Missing the 60-day loss-of-coverage SEP in Florida means you typically cannot enroll in a subsidized ACA Marketplace plan until the 2027 Open Enrollment Period, which runs November 1 through January 15 for coverage starting January 1, 2027. Florida Medicaid remains available year-round for categorically eligible Floridians (pregnant women, parents with very low income, people with disabilities) but most laid-off adults do not meet these requirements. If another qualifying life event occurs during the gap (moving to a new Florida county with different plan availability, getting married, having a baby), that event opens a new 60-day SEP. Short-term health plans are available but are not ACA-compliant, do not cover pre-existing conditions, and provide substantially less coverage than Marketplace plans.

es.question: Cual es la ventana del SEP despues de perder un trabajo en Florida en 2026?
es.answer: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial por perdida de cobertura comienza el dia despues de que termina su cobertura medica del empleador de Florida y dura 60 dias consecutivos. Por ejemplo, si su cobertura termina el 30 de junio de 2026, su ventana SEP es del 1 de julio al 29 de agosto de 2026. Envie su solicitud y seleccione un plan en healthcare.gov antes del dia 60. Los planes entran en vigor el primero del mes siguiente a su seleccion. Florida usa healthcare.gov (no hay intercambio estatal separado). Medicaid no tiene fecha limite SEP para floridanos categoricamente elegibles, pero la mayoria de adultos floridanos despedidos no califican para el Medicaid de Florida por la brecha de no expansion.

es.question: Cubre el Medicaid de Florida a los adultos despues de perder un trabajo?
es.answer: El Medicaid de Florida no cubre a la mayoria de adultos no mayores y no embarazados despues de perder un trabajo. Florida no expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA, por lo que el umbral estandar del 138% FPL basado en ingresos no aplica en Florida. El Medicaid de Florida esta disponible para: mujeres embarazadas hasta 196% FPL, padres de hijos menores con ingreso bajo aproximadamente 36% FPL, receptores de SSI y del Seguro Social de Discapacidad, y personas mayores o ciegas. Un adulto soltero o pareja sin hijos que perdio un trabajo en Florida casi con certeza no califica para el Medicaid de Florida. El SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov es la via de cobertura principal para la mayoria de adultos floridanos despedidos. Los adultos en la brecha de cobertura (0% a 100% FPL sin elegibilidad categorica) pueden acceder a planes Bronze con prima de $0 en healthcare.gov.

es.question: Que significa la brecha de cobertura del Medicaid de Florida para quienes pierden su trabajo?
es.answer: La brecha de cobertura del Medicaid de Florida se refiere a adultos con ingreso entre 0% y 100% FPL que no cumplen los requisitos categoricos del Medicaid de Florida (embarazo, discapacidad, crianza de hijos menores con bajos ingresos). En los estados de expansion, estos adultos obtendrian Medicaid gratuito. En Florida, no obtienen ni Medicaid ni subsidios ACA basados solo en ingresos. Sin embargo, las reglas del CMS permiten a los floridanos en la brecha de cobertura acceder a planes del Mercado Bronze con grandes subsidios o prima de $0 en healthcare.gov. Si su ingreso proyectado de 2026 cae por debajo del 100% FPL y no cumple los requisitos categoricos del Medicaid de Florida, solicite en healthcare.gov y seleccione el plan de menor costo disponible para su codigo postal de Florida.

es.question: Vale la pena COBRA despues de perder un trabajo en Florida?
es.answer: COBRA raramente es la mejor opcion financiera despues de perder un trabajo en Florida. COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa (parte del empleador mas la del empleado mas el 2% de tarifa administrativa). Para un residente individual de Florida, eso es tipicamente $500 a $900 al mes en 2026. Para una familia de Florida, a menudo llega a $1,200 a $2,800 al mes. Los planes del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales de prima tipicamente cuestan $10 a $300 al mes para floridanos de ingresos moderados. COBRA tiene sentido principalmente cuando tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista que no esta en ninguna red de planes del Mercado de Florida, o cuando su deducible de 2026 ya esta sustancialmente cumplido. Tiene 60 dias para elegir COBRA retroactivamente, dandole tiempo para comparar opciones en healthcare.gov primero.

es.question: Como pruebo la perdida de trabajo para la solicitud SEP en healthcare.gov en Florida?
es.answer: Healthcare.gov acepta su carta de terminacion del empleador de Florida, un aviso de eleccion COBRA, o un certificado de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA como documentacion del evento calificador de vida para el SEP por perdida de cobertura. El documento debe mostrar la fecha en que termino su cobertura del empleador. Cargue el documento cuando comience la solicitud SEP en healthcare.gov. Si aun no tiene el documento, comience la solicitud y cargue la documentacion despues, pero el reloj de 60 dias sigue corriendo. Contacte inmediatamente al departamento de recursos humanos de su antiguo empleador de Florida para solicitar la carta de terminacion y el certificado HIPAA por escrito.

es.question: Que es Florida KidCare y como ayuda despues de perder un trabajo?
es.answer: Florida KidCare es el programa CHIP de Florida que cubre a ninos menores de 19 anos con ingreso familiar hasta 200% FPL ($66,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026). La inscripcion es todo el ano en floridakidcare.org sin fecha limite. Florida KidCare tiene cuatro componentes: Medicaid para ninos bajo 133% FPL, MediKids para edades de 1 ano hasta kindergarten, Florida Healthy Kids para edad escolar hasta 18, y la Red de Servicios Medicos para Ninos para ninos con necesidades especiales. Despues de una perdida de trabajo en Florida, sus hijos pueden calificar para Florida KidCare incluso si usted esta en la brecha de cobertura del Medicaid de Florida. Las primas mensuales van de $0 a aproximadamente $20 segun los ingresos. Solicite en floridakidcare.org o a traves de healthcare.gov.

es.question: La Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida cuenta como ingreso para los subsidios ACA?
es.answer: Si. La Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida (el programa de compensacion por desempleo de Florida) cuenta como ingreso para los calculos del Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) del ACA en healthcare.gov. Incluya su beneficio semanal de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida multiplicado por el numero de semanas que espera recibirlo en su ingreso anual proyectado de 2026. El beneficio maximo semanal de Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida es $275 por hasta 12 semanas. Este ingreso afecta tanto el nivel de ingreso en el que cae para los calculos de subsidio como si puede cruzar el umbral del 100% FPL. Solicite la Asistencia de Reempleo de Florida en connect.myflorida.com y use la carta de beneficio como documentacion cuando solicite en healthcare.gov.

es.question: Que pasa si pierdo el SEP de 60 dias despues de perder mi trabajo en Florida?
es.answer: Perder el SEP de 60 dias por perdida de cobertura en Florida significa que tipicamente no puede inscribirse en un plan subsidiado del Mercado ACA hasta el Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta 2027, que corre del 1 de noviembre al 15 de enero para cobertura que comienza el 1 de enero de 2027. El Medicaid de Florida permanece disponible todo el ano para floridanos categoricamente elegibles, pero la mayoria de adultos despedidos no cumplen estos requisitos. Si ocurre otro evento calificador de vida durante la brecha (mudarse a un nuevo condado de Florida con diferente disponibilidad de planes, casarse, tener un bebe), ese evento abre un nuevo SEP de 60 dias. Los planes de salud a corto plazo estan disponibles pero no son compatibles con el ACA y no cubren condiciones preexistentes.
